items.title: Is CrowdStrike Stock A Buy Today As AI Threats Lift Demand?
items.summary: The popular view of CrowdStrike (CRWD) is that AI has made a fast-growing security company grow even faster. The stock returned 98% over the past year. The S&P 500 returned 18.5% over the same period. For that view to be right, two things must both be true. The faster growth has to last, and it has to turn into real profit. So far, only the first one clearly holds.

items.title: S&P 500 Valuation Is Really A Mega-Cap Problem
items.summary: The Hennessy Funds portfolio manager argues that market-cap weighting can hide cheaper mid-cap stocks, but investors still need a process for weighing valuation, business improvement, and price confirmation.

items.title: Has The Price For Amazon Stock Already Peaked?
items.summary: The market has rewarded this tech giant for its powerful business engine, but a recent pullback forces investors to ask if the best part of the run is already over.

items.title: How Far Could Zoom Communications Stock Fall In A Real Market Shock?
items.summary: Zoom Communications (ZM) stock sits about 21% below its 52-week high after falling 17.4% over the past month, a month in which its quarterly report beat its own guidance. Over the past year it returned 2.9% while the S&P 500 returned 17.3%. The question for a holder is what a real market shock would add.

items.title: Is MercadoLibre Stock As Cheap As Its Cash Says?
items.summary: MercadoLibre (MELI) produced free cash flow worth 13.7% of its market value over the past twelve months, about three times the 4.5% yield of the median S&P 500 company. A yield that high usually marks either a bargain or a business the market expects to shrink. MercadoLibre fits neither neatly. Its revenue grew 46% over the same twelve months, and management is holding profit down on purpose to keep it growing.

items.title: How Low Can UiPath Stock Go When Its Numbers Are Not The Problem?
items.summary: UiPath (PATH) trades at about $14, some 29% below its high of the past year, and it has lost 11.7% over the past month. Its results are not what did that. The fall is recent: the stock is still up 34.5% over the past three months, and over the past twelve months it returned 18.9% against 17.0% for the S&P 500. What matters is how far a stock like this falls in a real shock.
